title: artifact-semver-conflict-debug-log
content:
Purpose
Quick scratchpad for the partial rollback we attempted Nov 7–8 to mitigate a canary failure that surfaced after promoting service-api v1.5.0. This is a personal timeline + commands + outputs + hypotheses record so anyone can reconstruct what I tried and why we reverted the way we did. Not polished — notes to self.

Symptom summary
- At 2025-11-07 17:12 UTC, canary route (5% traffic) for service-api reported 15% increase in 4xx for /v1/predict and several 500s.
- Error pattern: clients started seeing 400 JSON validation errors for requests that previously worked. No schema changes were in the client.
- Cross-check: latency stable, no notable CPU/GPU spikes on pods; only error rate spiked.

Quick hypothesis (first-pass)
- semver mismatch: artifact annotated as 1.5.0 but build packaging may have pulled a library with a breaking change (schema lib bumped minor).
- release pipeline promoted an image tagged 1.5.0 that contains an unintended migration/feature flag default (new strict parser).
- CDN or traffic shaping not at fault — errors are immediate upon request probing a fresh canary pod.

Timeline (local timestamps)
- 2025-11-07 16:40 UTC — CI job ci-service-api/build-91234 succeeded; image pushed to registry with tag 1.5.0 and digest sha256:5f6a7c8d9e0b.
- 2025-11-07 16:55 UTC — Release pipeline (promote-to-canary) started, Argo rollouts created 3 canary pods.
- 2025-11-07 17:12 UTC — Monitoring alert triggered for 4xx increase.
- 2025-11-07 17:18 UTC — First canary pod logs show rapid JSON.parse errors.
- 2025-11-07 17:30 UTC — Attempted traffic dial-down to 0% for canary.
- 2025-11-07 17:45 UTC — Triggered rollback to previous stable (1.4.2) on canary set, observed normalized error rates by 17:58.

Commands I ran (copied from terminal)
- Inspect image metadata and digests:
  gcloud artifacts docker images describe gcr.io/redwood-release/service-api:1.5.0 --project=redwood-release --format=json
  # output contained digest: sha256:5f6a7c8d9e0b and build-id 91234

- Confirm image contents (quick container run):
  docker pull gcr.io/redwood-release/service-api@sha256:5f6a7c8d9e0b
  docker run --rm -it gcr.io/redwood-release/service-api@sha256:5f6a7c8d9e0b /bin/bash -c 'ls -la /app && cat /app/requirements.txt | grep schema'
  # observed schema-lib==2.0.0 in container, previous stable 1.4.2 contained schema-lib==1.8.1

- Check Helm/Argo rollout resource and annotations:
  kubectl -n prod get rollout service-api -o yaml | sed -n '1,200p'
  # annotation: released-by: pipeline/promote-to-canary/ci-91234

- Looked for migration flags in envvars in the pod:
  kubectl -n prod exec -it <canary-pod> -- printenv | grep -E 'FEATURE|MIGRATION|STRICT'
  # found: FEATURE_STRICT_SCHEMA=1 (not expected for canary)

Observed error snippets (copied from logs)
- 2025-11-07T17:13:04Z service-api-canary-0 stderr: ERROR request=abcd123 body="{\"input\":{...}}" err="schema.ValidationError: expected object, got string at /payload/userId"
- 2025-11-07T17:13:05Z service-api-canary-1 stderr: WARN parser: unknown field 'strictMode' ; defaulting to false
- 2025-11-07T17:13:06Z service-api-canary-1 stderr: ERROR Unhandled exception: TypeError: Cannot read property 'trim' of undefined

What I checked quickly and ruled out
- Client regression: quick trace of a failing request showed the same body shape as previously successful requests (curl test confirmed).
- Env diff across clusters: stable pods don't have FEATURE_STRICT_SCHEMA set.
- Network/proxy: no change to ingress config; health checks succeeded.

Root-cause working theory
- Build step for 1.5.0 inadvertently baked a parent image layer that upgraded schema-lib from 1.8.x to 2.0.0. The 2.0.0 version enforces a stricter validation by default when FEATURE_STRICT_SCHEMA is present (or defaulted true) and the release pipeline also set that envvar in the canary manifest due to a templating bug. Combined, these caused requests with optional string fields to be rejected.

Why semver confusion happened
- CI pipeline uses semver tag from package.json + docker build cache. A shared dependency image (base-python) was rebuilt upstream and pulled at build time (no lockfile existed for that layer). The build recorded 1.5.0 but didn't pin transitive library versions.

Immediate remediation steps taken (chronological)
1) Scoped traffic back to zero for canary (Argo rollouts trafficWeight=0) to reduce user impact.
2) Replaced canary image with stable digest 1.4.2 (pinned digest) in the rollout config and rolled forward the canary set to validate: kubectl -n prod set image deployment/service-api service-api=gcr.io/redwood-release/service-api@sha256:3b2c4d6e7f8a
3) Monitored errors — rate returned to baseline in ~13 minutes.
4) Opened JIRA ENGOPS-2529 with initial notes and linking offending build artifacts.

Notes on rollback vs rollforward decision
- We chose to pin the canary back to the last known-good digest (rollforward to previous image) instead of performing a rollback at the pipeline level because the artifact registry contained an immutable digest for stable 1.4.2 and we could revert the deployment quickly.
- We left the pipeline failure window open and paused further promotions until a root cause is verified.

Commands used to pin the image during remediation
- kubectl -n prod set image deployment/service-api service-api=gcr.io/redwood-release/service-api@sha256:3b2c4d6e7f8a --record
- kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/service-api --timeout=120s

Follow-up investigations (next actions)
- Add lockfile or pin transitive libs during docker build (Action: infra/ci to add pip/poetry lock/constraints).
- Change release promotion to always use digest (not mutable tag) as the source of truth for deployments. Confirm Argo/Helm templates accept digest-only images.
- Add a pre-promote smoke test that runs a minimal request through the canary image and checks JSON acceptance for a set of sample payloads.
- Add a CI job to diff installed package versions between base image and built image and fail on major version bumps for critical libs.
- Audit templating logic that injected FEATURE_STRICT_SCHEMA into canary envs; track down which pipeline task set it.

Short-term tasks assigned
- Ethan to paste final log excerpts into JIRA ENGOPS-2529 and attach the failing container tarball (done).
- Lin to create a small CI gate that validates the JSON parser behavior against the existing test corpus (in progress).
- Priya to update release playbook to prefer digest pins for rollouts and document the emergency rollback steps (next week).

Loose notes / things I thought of but didn't verify yet
- Could the base-image cache on the build node be stale and cause inconsistent transitive deps across identical tags? Need to verify builder caches.
- Check whether our semantic-release tooling bumped package metadata without updating the lockfile in the repo.
- Consider a canary hook that samples 100 requests through the canary and runs acceptance checks before dialing up.

Appendix: useful one-liners I saved here
- List all images with digests: gcloud artifacts docker images list gcr.io/redwood-release --project=redwood-release --format='get(name,digest,tags)'
- Compare installed packages inside two images:
  docker run --rm gcr.io/redwood-release/service-api@sha256:5f6a7c8d9e0b pip freeze | sort > /tmp/new.txt
  docker run --rm gcr.io/redwood-release/service-api@sha256:3b2c4d6e7f8a pip freeze | sort > /tmp/old.txt
  diff -u /tmp/old.txt /tmp/new.txt | head -n 200

End of scratchpad — keep this in the users folder as a single-source incident breadcrumb for anyone doing a postmortem.
